annotations.title: See what is on a page worth filming

description: [Free] Opens a public page in a real browser and ranks what a video could film — calls to action, images, cards, pricing, testimonials, search boxes, headings — each with a CSS selector, kind, size and score (a rank, not a percentage). Says when a robot check, sign-in or missing page stood in front of it (blocked, block_kind), and which fields will never be typed into.

aspect_ratio.description: The viewport to look through. 9:16 loads the page as a phone does, which is the layout a vertical video films — a responsive site offers different elements there (a sticky call bar, stacked cards) and they score differently.

kinds.description: Comma-separated kinds to keep, e.g. "cta,search,card". The vocabulary is in the `kinds` histogram of any reply: cta, media, image, card, pricing, testimonial, logos, heading, section, nav, search, chat, input. Omitted, every kind is offered.

limit.description: How many candidates to return, best first (a page offers up to 40; a film uses four or five). The `kinds` histogram still counts every one.

url.description: A public page to look at. Nothing is filmed and no credit is spent.

name: inspect_page

centrable.description: Whether the camera can put this subject in the middle of the frame. false for the outer columns of a grid: the window never leaves the page, so an edge card is framed against the page edge with its neighbour showing. Prefer true for a spotlight; a wide subject is always true.

pages.description: The other pages of this site a film may be sent to, taken from this page's own links. A scene's page_url is DROPPED unless it is one of these or the page itself, so this is the complete set — not a suggestion.

refused_fields.description: selector, label, reason: fields never typed into.

title: See what is on a page worth filming
